findings.text: blocking: the attempt-naming refusal built at promotion.py:264 is discarded by the caller every promotion goes through — `_remove_promoted_pointer_or_defer` catches the CrewError at :469 and either returns False or re-raises its own attempt-free text at :493 — so no promotion-level refusal names the launch that kept the pointer, which is the whole of the done_when's third case; tests/test_an_ended_attempt_holds_nothing.py:308 passes only because it calls the private `_remove_promoted_pointer` directly, a call site production reaches only through the wrapper that drops the message.

non-blocking: `_reserved_attempt_ended` at reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2734 re-implements the strict attempt-receipt read inline — json.loads, Mapping check, run-id equality — duplicating `_run_exit_record(..., require_run_id=True)` at reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1534 rather than extending that owner with the directory argument the fix needed, while the module's own `_retired_attempt_ended` at dispatch_launch.py:2238 still routes through the owner, so two readings of one receipt can diverge without either failing.

non-blocking: the fragment states the after arm ran at `f5f4675488`, while arms/after.log line 1 records `# revision: 63181b9c75` and manifest.md's after_suite records 63181b9c75 too, so the record a reader checks before promotion disagrees with the log it cites about which revision was measured.
